answer: When a new agent joins, it must stake a cryptographic “ocean” bond that is locked for a random “dune” period drawn from a verifiable random function; only after the bond matures does a lantern‑style referral reward become claimable, and the reward is zero unless the recruiter’s own stake remains unspent. An attacker creating a Sybil must purchase and lock one ocean bond per fake identity and wait the full dune interval before any reward can be harvested, inflating the cost by the bond amount plus the opportunity cost of the lock‑up time.
